transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Yes, thank you for seeing me. I suppose... well, the main thing, the reason I’m sitting here today, is that my sleep has just become completely unmoored. I mean, absolutely detached from any sort of normal human rhythm. 

It’s been quite a progression, really, and quite distressing. At first, a little while ago, I actually thought it was a stroke of good fortune. I’d go to bed, and then after only two or three hours, I would be wide awake. But not just awake—I felt entirely ready to go. I’d get up in the dead of night and go straight to my desk to start drafting plans. I have my graduate degrees, you know, and even though I’m retired and out of the workforce now, I had all these sudden, expansive ideas for projects and proposals. I was just writing and drafting for hours in the dark, feeling fantastic, completely energized. 

But... well, that’s not what is happening now. The whole thing has shifted into something else entirely. I still can't sleep, but instead of that wonderful energy, I just lie awake in the pitch black, hours before dawn. I just lie there staring at the ceiling, and my stomach is so terribly tight, just completely knotted up. There's absolutely no sense of rest anymore. None at all. I get out of bed feeling just as wretched as when I got in, but I simply cannot sleep, and it’s just dragging on and on, night after night, and I just don't know how to turn it off.
Have there been other times in your life when you felt unusually energetic, maybe even needing less sleep, along with an elevated or irritable mood, not just during this recent period?

Well, yes, actually. Now that you frame it that way... it hasn't just been this recent spell with the drafting and the midnight projects. 

There was a time, oh, quite a while back, where for weeks on end—and I mean weeks, not just a passing good mood or a couple of productive days—I felt almost... well, brilliantly optimistic. It was this profound sense of clarity, really. I felt as if every single obstacle in my path was completely trivial. You know how most people get bogged down by the logistics of life? The mundane details, the red tape, the reasons why things *can't* be done? I looked at all of that and just laughed. It all seemed so incredibly easy to manage. I was walking around feeling like I had the absolute key to the universe in my pocket, just brimming with this unshakeable confidence. 

But the problem—and this is where it gets rather complicated, and where I suppose I caused quite a bit of friction—was how I reacted to other people during that time. Because I was operating on this incredibly high, efficient frequency, anyone who didn't immediately see my vision... well, I had absolutely zero patience for them. 

If anyone questioned me, even just a simple, innocuous question about what I was doing or why I was moving so fast, I snapped at them. I mean, I was viciously sharp. I felt like they were deliberately trying to sabotage me. It was as if I was the only sensible man in the room, the only one who actually understood how things ought to be done, and everyone else was just dragging their feet, asking foolish questions just to drag me down to their level of mediocrity. I remember one specific conversation where I just... well, I completely tore into an old friend because he suggested I might be taking on too much. I just couldn't tolerate the interference. It’s strange looking back at it now, how quickly that brilliant, shining optimism could turn into such a fierce, defensive anger the second I felt contradicted. But yes, to answer your question, it was a very distinct period of time.
After that period of intense energy and optimism, did you go through a time where you felt deeply down, hopeless, or experienced a major loss of interest in things you usually enjoy?

Well, yes... yes, that's exactly what happens. It’s like a pendulum swinging from one extreme to the other, but the swing back is so incredibly heavy. After that period of just... soaring, feeling like I could conquer the world, the crash was profound. And I mean profound. It wasn't just feeling a bit blue or having a bad week. It was like all the color was completely drained out of my life, just siphoned away until everything was a dull, flat gray. 

And the worst part of it, the part that really frightens me when I think about it, is the complete and utter loss of interest in... well, in everything that makes life worth living. I’ve always been a man of varied interests, you see. I used to spend whole afternoons at the art museum downtown, just wandering the galleries, examining the brushstrokes, really absorbing the history. Or I’d lose myself in my photography—I have a lovely old Leica that I used to take everywhere, waiting for the perfect light. And cooking, too! I used to love spending hours preparing a complex meal, sourcing the ingredients, the whole ritual of it. 

But lately... during these dark spells... I look at my camera sitting on the shelf, or I think about going down to the bridge club where I’ve played for years, and I feel absolutely nothing. Nothing at all. There’s no spark, no anticipation. The only thing I feel is an overwhelming sense of exhaustion at the mere thought of the effort it would take to even pretend I care. It’s just... it’s like a heavy blanket is thrown over my mind, and I can't even muster the energy to lift a corner of it to see the world outside. I just sit in my chair, staring out the window, and the hours just slip by, and I couldn't care less. It’s a terrible, hollow feeling, Doctor. Just terrible.
Doctor: Was there ever a time when this elevated mood and increased energy lasted for a full week or more without needing to sleep, or did it always eventually give way to the low mood before that?

Well, as for how long it lasted... yes, it certainly went on for more than a week. Much more. In fact, if I really trace it back to the genesis of the whole ordeal, it all started after a rather significant financial blow. I had made an investment—a very calculated one, mind you, based on extensive research and what I thought were foolproof projections. But the market, as they say, has a mind of its own, and the loss was... substantial. 

And instead of just accepting it, I suppose something inside me just snapped into this frantic overdrive. For about five months—yes, five whole months—I wasn't myself at all. I wasn't the retired gentleman enjoying his bridge club and his photography. I was completely consumed. My entire existence revolved around trying to undo the damage, to recoup the loss. I was up at all hours, as I mentioned, drafting these elaborate schemes, convinced I could outsmart the market, outsmart the brokers. I didn't need sleep, I didn't need rest, I just needed to fix it. It was a solid five months of this relentless, burning drive before the bottom finally fell out and I crashed into that terrible grayness I described. So, yes, a week is an understatement. It was a season of my life, entirely hijacked by this... this absolute frenzy.

During those periods of intense energy and confidence, did you ever experience things like hearing voices, seeing things that others couldn’t see, or believing things that weren’t based in reality—like having special powers or being on a mission from a higher power?

Well, no... no, nothing quite like that. I mean, I certainly felt like I had a unique insight, a sort of unparalleled clarity about the markets and my investments, as I was telling you. I felt like I could see patterns that the so-called experts were entirely blind to. But it wasn't a... a mystical revelation or anything of that sort. 

I wasn't receiving messages from God or the universe, and I certainly wasn't hearing any disembodied voices whispering in my ear while I was at my desk at three in the morning. I was just... profoundly, deeply convinced of my own intellectual superiority in that moment. I felt like a grandmaster looking at a chessboard while everyone else was playing checkers. But I never saw things that weren't there, no apparitions or hallucinations. 

My reality was just... amplified, I suppose you could say. The volume was turned all the way up on my own thoughts, so much so that they drowned out any common sense or external advice. But it was still just me in my study, surrounded by my papers and my charts. I didn't believe I had magical powers, just an extraordinary, albeit exhausting, capacity for work and analysis. So, no, no voices or visions, just that overwhelming, relentless drive.
